page: UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-128GB-2xL40S is an accelerated cloud server instance designed for artificial intelligence, machine learning, and graphics processing. The instance features 12 vCPUs and 12 physical cores operating on an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz within a KVM hypervisor. Memory capacity totals 128 GB of RAM, equating to 10.67 GB per core. Acceleration is delivered by two NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L40S GPUs providing a cumulative 96 GB of VRAM. The server does not bundle local disk storage, necessitating network-attached storage configurations, and comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier single-core CPU throughput, highlighted by a stress-ng single-core score of 4216.38 and a Geekbench single-core result of 2805.0. Vector instruction processing is supported via AVX-512 extensions including VNNI and BF16. Multi-core performance registers within the strong bracket, posting 16921.0 on Geekbench and a 41242.51 PassMark CPU score. Large-block memory transfers achieve strong throughput, delivering 308.18 GB/s on reads and 161.95 GB/s on writes. For AI inference workloads, the dual L40S architecture achieves top-tier results in small-model text generation at 368.6 tokens/s and strong prompt processing throughput at 3357.72 tokens/s, while medium 7B model generation yields 35.15 tokens/s.

In terms of resource allocation, the platform balances substantial dual-GPU acceleration with moderate host compute density. The 96 GB total GPU frame buffer enables deployment of multi-billion parameter foundation models and batch image generation without dedicating excessive CPU overhead. The lack of integrated local storage shifts persistence requirements to external volumes, representing a technical tradeoff for IO-heavy operations. The server is well matched for LLM inference, AI fine-tuning, neural rendering, visual computing pipelines, and accelerated scientific data analysis.

Operating on a KVM hypervisor, the x86_64 system includes advanced vector acceleration via AVX-512 and AVX-VNNI flags. The instance contains no bundled local storage, requiring attached volumes for persistent data. In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates top-tier single-core metrics, registering 2805.0 on Geekbench, alongside strong memory bandwidth of 308.18 GB/s on uncached reads. AI inference capabilities reach 368.6 tokens per second for small-model generation and 35.15 tokens per second for 7B parameters. The hardware profile is engineered for generative AI inference, deep learning model fine-tuning, batch graphics rendering, and accelerated computing workloads.
